overview: This 370-page file documents Japanese exhibitions and U.S. responses from 1931 to 1938. Its main subjects are the 1933 Tokyo Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition, the 1935 Yokohama exposition, the 1937 Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition, and the proposed 1940 Tokyo exposition. Invitations, diplomatic correspondence, consular reports, plans, and exhibitor materials trace American participation, publicity efforts, international recruitment, and postponement.
interest: The file shows how exhibition diplomacy worked in practice, from official invitations and funding limits to publicity and on-site assessments.
